entries.title: Exodus 33:3
segments: I will not go; not go with his visible, special presence, but would send an Angel to lead them, as stated

entries.title: Exodus 33:4
segments: No created beings and no earthly enjoyments can be an adequate substitute for the presence and favor of God.  Without him as our friend and portion, however many other things we may have, we shall ultimately be wretched.

entries.title: Exodus 33:5
segments:
I will--consume thee; this he might justly do; and this, should they continue their wickedness, he would do.  We may, however, render these words, If I come up into the midst of thee for one moment, I shall consume thee. 
 
  Therefore now put off thy ornaments; he will have them put themselves in the dress of criminals, while he, as it were, deliberates what he shall do to them.

entries.title: Exodus 33:6
segments: By the mount Horeb; or, at a distance from the mount Horeb.

entries.title: Exodus 33:7
segments:
The tabernacle; not the holy tent for the building of which directions had been given, for that was not yet made; but probably the public tent of the congregation, where Moses had been accustomed to hear causes, and where also, before the arrival at Sinai, he had received communications from God. 
 
  Without the camp; implying that the people's sins had cut them off from the privilege of having God's presence in the camp. 
 
  The Tabernacle of the congregation; the place where the penitent of the congregaiton should assemble, and where God would meet them. 
 
If men would find mercy and obtain the favor of God, they must seek him while he is to be found, and call upon him while he is near; repent of their sins, forsake their evil ways, and turn heartily to him: then he will abundantly pardon.

entries.title: Exodus 33:10
segments: Worshipped; bowed themselves in token of worshipping Jehovah, who was in the cloudy pillar.

entries.title: Exodus 33:11
segments: Departed not out of the tabernacle; he seems to have remained in charge of it.

entries.title: Exodus 33:12
segments: Thou hast not let me know; he had only told him he would send an Angel before them,

; and Moses wished for more information, especially that God, by his own presence, would go with them. 
 
  By name; as his intimate and peculiar friend.

entries.title: Exodus 33:13
segments: Thy way; God's way of dealing with men, including his purposes and will respecting Israel,
.  This prayer is nearly related to that in

. 
 
Clear views of the will and ways of God are earnestly desired by his people; especially such views as shall make plain the path of duty, and prepare them faithfully to walk in it.

entries.title: Exodus 33:14
segments:
My presence shall go; in the pillar of cloud and of fire, to guide and protect them.  Thus the prayer of Moses was answered. 
 
  Give thee rest; thee and thy people.

entries.title: Exodus 33:16
segments: Thou goest with us? in the cloudy pillar, thus showing that they were his people, and he was their God.

entries.title: Exodus 33:17
segments: The number and greatness of the favors which God has bestowed, may be pleaded as a reason why he should bestow still more and greater.  When rightly improved, the more numerous they are the more numerous will be those which shall follow.

entries.title: Exodus 33:18
segments: Show me thy glory; Moses asks and receives such a visible manifestation of Jehovah's glory as is at the same time a revelation of his glorious character and attributes. See

entries.title: Exodus 33:19
segments:
The name of the Lord; his glorious attributes; for his name is the sum of these. 
 
  Be gracious--show mercy; his sovereignty in dealing with sinners, which is always guided by infinite wisdom and goodness, is a part of his glory.

entries.title: Exodus 33:20
segments: My face; that is, my face when I appear to thee in my glory.  In conversing with Moses face to face, God had veiled his glory, that his servant might not be overwhelmed by its brightness.

entries.title: Exodus 33:21
segments: By me; on Sinai.

entries.title: Exodus 33:22
segments: Passeth by; in visible form, and, as appears from
, in the form of man.  It was the eternal Word that made to Moses this revelation,
; and it was an anticipation of the glory in which he now reveals himself at the right hand of the Father.  Compare

entries.title: Exodus 33:23
segments: However great the manifestations of the glory of God, his people desire to see more; and they will see more, and still more, as their blessedness and usefulness may require.  But however much they may see, and however long their knowledge may continue to increase, it will only increase their sense of the infinitude of what remains unseen.
